[MATH: A \times B = \big\{(a, b) \: : \: a \in A,\, b \in B \big\}]

To visualize [MATH: S], consider [MATH: S_1\subset S] containing all points whose [MATH: x]-coordinate equals [MATH: {\color{red}{1}}] and whose [MATH: y]-coordinate is any real number in the interval [MATH: (0,1).]

[MATH: S_1 = \Big\{ ({\color{red}{1}},y) \: : \: y \in(0,1) \Big\}]

[MATH: S_2 = \big\{ ({\color{blue}{2}},y) \: : \: y \in(0,1) \big\}.]

This set is represented by the line segment shown below.

Our Cartesian product is the union of these subsets:

[MATH: S = S_1\cup S_2]

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Recall that if [MATH: A] and [MATH: B] are sets, the Cartesian product [MATH: A \times B] consists of all ordered pairs [MATH: (a,b)] whose first coordinate belongs to [MATH: A] and whose second coordinate belongs to [MATH: B.]

Content:
[MATH: A \times B = \big\{(a, b) \: : \: a \in A,\, b \in B \big\}]

Content:
Many Cartesian products have natural representations in the Cartesian plane. The most common of these is the Cartesian product [MATH: \mathbb R^2{:}]

Content:
[MATH: \mathbb R^2 = \mathbb R\times\mathbb R = \big\{(x, y) \: : \: x,y \in \mathbb R \big\}]

Content:
This infinite set contains all ordered pairs [MATH: (x,y),] where [MATH: x] and [MATH: y] can be any real numbers. In other words, [MATH: \mathbb R^2] contains every point in the Cartesian plane!
